symbols.name: OPN_R
symbols.role: round open, multiply the state by alpha

symbols.name: CLS_R
symbols.role: round close, multiply the state by alpha inverse

symbols.name: OPN_S
symbols.role: square open, multiply the state by alpha

symbols.name: CLS_S
symbols.role: square close, multiply the state by alpha inverse

provenance.source: section 1 and 2 of the LingoLOGOS ASIC specification, GF(2^8) automaton
semantics: The state is a field element. Reading a bracket multiplies the state by that symbol
multiplier in GF(2^8) modulo 0x11D, so the state after a word w is the product of the
multipliers of its letters, and the initial state 0x01 is reached again exactly when the
number of open brackets equals the number of close brackets, modulo the order of alpha.
The compiler enumerates the reachable states from the initial state, computes every
transition with field arithmetic, and emits the closed table as a unique case netlist.
alpha = 0x02 has multiplicative order 255, so the closure is the whole nonzero field:
255 states, 1020 transitions for the four declared symbols.
known_limitations: The automaton recognizes the commutative image of Dyck-2, not Dyck-2: it accepts the
crossed words (] and ][ because multiplication commutes, so the bracket classes cannot
be distinguished by any GF(2^8) multiplier pair with equal and inverse values.
Because alpha has order 255, a word with 255 more opens than closes also returns to the
initial state, so the count invariant is modulo 255 and not exact.
A finite automaton on 256 states cannot recognize Dyck-2 at all: the language needs an
unbounded stack (Myhill-Nerode), so a bounded-depth prefix invariant is the strongest
property any automaton of this size can check.
